decisionsTitle: Invitations by email: a place kept for a named person until a deadline, accepted through the form
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-02**, with the 21 November race full (150 places, a capped waiting list): «După ce rezolvăm, vreau să trimit „invitații speciale” pe email pentru membrii BVR, un fel de adaugă manual.» — and, a message later, «Dar vreau și pentru non-membrii.» The club wants to seat chosen people — members, partners, guests — by sending each a personal invitation, rather than asking them to fight the public form or having staff type their whole registration («Adaugă o înscriere», §33, which needs the person's request relayed and every field). He was told the design below and did not object; the dispatcher launched it with these defaults while he is away.

**Decision.** An Administrator invites named people to one event from its registrations list, section «Invitații» (`registrations/ui/InvitationsPanel.tsx`, `InviteForm.tsx`): members ticked from the members' zone accounts (§524; any role, with a search), and/or people typed one per line — the name, then the address (`parseInvitationLines`) — plus «Zile până expiră» (7 by default, 1 to 60) and «În afara locurilor». Each person gets one email, `EVENT_INVITATION`, in the member account's language or else Romanian: the club, the event and its start, until when the place is kept, «Acceptă invitația», and «dacă nu te așteptai la acest email, ignoră-l». The link opens the event's own registration form, prefilled: the name, the address said back and locked, «Sunt membru» ticked for a member; every other field, the consents (terms, privacy notice, fitness, the list, the offers) and the declaration stay the person's. The section lists every invitation — name, address, state (trimisă / acceptată → the registration / expirată / retrasă), deadline, who sent it — with «Retrimite» and «Retrage» on the open ones; the editor's «Înscrierile primite» says «invitații în așteptare: N» and links to the section.

**The data.** `event_invitations` (migration `0124`): the event, the address's participant, the name and the address as typed, the canonical address (§10.4), the language, the member's account, who sent it, `sent_at`, `expires_at`, `outside_capacity`, `supplementary_raise`, `accepted_at` + `accepted_registration_id`, `withdrawn_at` + who, `expired_at`, `resend_count`, `last_sent_at`. **The state is three stamps and the deadline, not a status column**: live = none stamped and `expires_at` ahead; the count compares `expires_at` on every read (§10.6), and the maintenance sweep writes `expired_at` afterwards for the backoffice, the link's page and the partial unique index (one open invitation per address per event). Enum values (migration `0125`, expand only): `email_message_type` + `EVENT_INVITATION`, `email_action_token_purpose` + `ACCEPT_INVITATION`.

**The link** (§12.8, BR-REQ-036-02). `email_action_tokens` gains a nullable `invitation_id`: an `ACCEPT_INVITATION` token is scoped to the invitation and to the participant of its address, with no registration — none exists yet. The CHECK that tied «no registration» to `MANAGE_PROFILE` now admits this purpose too (compared as text, so the migration names no enum value it adds), a second CHECK ties the purpose to the invitation, the participant-scope unique index leaves invitation tokens out, and a new partial unique index keeps one live link per invitation. **Choice: the address's participant row is written at the send** (`findOrCreateParticipant`), because a token needs one; the retention's orphan sweep leaves a participant with an invitation alone, and an ended invitation's deletion takes the row with it when nothing else holds it. The token is minted at the send (`notifications/invitation-render.ts`), hashed at rest; it lives until the invitation's deadline plus thirty days, so the page can say why it no longer works; whether it may still register is the invitation's own state, asked under the event lock. The GET (`/[locale]/registrations/invitation/[token]`) only reads (read-only transaction): the form, or «folosită», «retrasă», «expirată», «există un email mai nou» (§619) or the generic refusal, each with the contact page.

**Accepting.** The press (`registrations/invitations.ts#acceptInvitation`) locks the event, spends the token (single use, one UPDATE), asks the invitation again — open and before its deadline — and creates the registration through the one door, `submitRegistration`, with an origin `invitation`: the address is the invitation's whatever is posted; no anti-bot check, no full-line refusal, no family flow (one person per invitation, the staff entry's name rule `via: "staff"` — this runner again on the address is refused, anybody else within the club's limit); the public window's opening and the members-only door are not asked (the invitation is the door; the event must still be local, scheduled, dated and published); and **no verification email** — the link proved the inbox, so `seatInvitedRegistration` writes the participant's own `email_verified_at`, copies «În afara locurilor» from the invitation, and asks the one allocator for the place with the invitation's flag (`allocateOrWaitlist`'s `invited`, like a family's reserved place): the registration becomes `PENDING_DECLARATION` with the ordinary deadline (§104) and its `COMPLETE_DECLARATION` email, **while the invitation still counts**, and only then is the invitation marked accepted — the place moves from the invitation's bucket to the hold in one transaction, with no instant where it is free. A refused form (a field, the terms changed, this runner on the address) rolls the token's spend back with everything else: the same link still works. Audited `event.invitation_accepted` (no actor).

**The formula** (`AGENTS.md` §10.6). `countOccupied` gains `invitationHolds`: live invitations, not «În afara locurilor», before their deadline; `computeOccupied` adds them, so the public line, `publicFill`, the free places, the queue panel and §589's sentence («… invitați {invited}») see them as taken; «Cine vine (N)» is unchanged — nobody is confirmed yet. **Why the club's choice**: like a family's reservation (§543), an invitation is never released for somebody waiting before its deadline — the club named this person and told them until when — only at the deadline (`expireStaleHolds` → `expireLapsedInvitations`, which every capacity-changing transaction runs first; the maintenance job selects an event with a lapsed one and is woken for the nearest deadline) or at «Retrage»; either way the place goes to the line as the event's setting says (`fillAvailableSpots`). `kind` is in no condition.

**Sending** (`service.ts#inviteToEventByStaff`, through `admin-service.ts#inviteToEvent`, the action `invitation-actions.ts#inviteAction`). The Administrator's alone, asserted in all three. One transaction for the whole list under the event lock: the event local, scheduled, published, dated, not started, its registration not closed; the line served first (`fillAvailableSpots`, as `placeForNewcomer`); each address canonicalized and refused, **by the person's name, nothing written**, when it already holds a registration in a live state, an open invitation, or appears twice; the deadline `min(now + days, close, start)`. **On a full race (§642)** each invitation that needs a counted place and finds none adds one supplementary place (`addOneSupplementaryPlace`, audited `event.capacity_raised_for_invitation` with the invitation's id) — only when the form carried exactly the locked capacity plus that number (`invitationRaises`, `confirmsInvitationRaises`), which the dialog names before the press: «{n} invitații. Locuri libere acum: {free}. Se adaugă {k} locuri suplimentare: capacitatea devine {cap}.», the button «Adaugă {k} locuri și trimite», or «Niciun loc nou». Any other number refuses the whole send with `SUPPLEMENTARY_PLACE_UNCONFIRMED`. An invitation never takes a lapsed declaration hold's place (§160): that runner may still sign, and the club's addition is the visible one. **«În afara locurilor» (§643)** at the send: the invitations hold no counted place and need none, and the registration the link creates is outside the places too. Audited `event.invitation_sent` by the invitation's id (deadline, outside, whether a place was added) — never the name or the address.

**Resend and withdraw.** «Retrimite» (`resendInvitationByStaff`): a new email and link — the old link superseded (§619) — the deadline kept, or moved to the days typed from now when that is later (never earlier), `resend_count + 1`, audited. «Retrage» (`withdrawInvitationByStaff`): withdrawn now, the place offered to the line in the same transaction, audited; the link's page says withdrawn. Both under the event lock, both refused on an invitation no longer open.

**Privacy and retention.** The privacy notice's template (both languages, section 2) gains one paragraph under `{{eventInvitations}}` — filled with the section's own name, «Invitații»: an Administrator may enter a person's name and address to send one invitation, legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)); kept until accepted, withdrawn or expired, then as the registration's data or deleted like an unconfirmed registration (section 7). `/admin/tasks` carries the row `invitationsNotice` (open, never blocking) until a notice naming it is in force in every language; **the flow is allowed meanwhile**, as §389's registering of another person on one's own address was. The email carries its own privacy line («… ți-a trecut numele și adresa ca să te invite»). The retention job (`jobs/retention.ts`, step `invitations`) deletes an invitation that ended unaccepted — withdrawn, or past its deadline whether stamped or not (a cancelled event's are never swept) — thirty days after it ended (the window of an unconfirmed registration), with its link, then the orphaned participant; an accepted one goes with its registration.

**Refused.** A registration created by staff without the person — the declaration and the consents are theirs, and «Adaugă o înscriere» already exists for a relayed request. A public invitation code — anybody could pass it on, and it would name nobody. An invitation that bypasses the capacity without a confirmed place — overbooking by another name (BR-REQ-034-01). The address from a query string — the link carries only the token. A status column — a deadline is evaluated on every read, and a column the sweep forgot would keep a place nobody holds. Taking a lapsed declaration hold for an invitation — see above. Emailing the invitee when the invitation expires — the email said the deadline.

**Not done, recorded as follow-ups.** The automatic emails' forecast (§516) does not foresee the offer an invitation's lapse makes to the line. The registration's page does not yet say a registration came from an invitation (the invitation row names it, the section links it).

**Tests.** `tests/integration/registrations/invitations.test.ts` (new): the held place in the count and the public line from the send, the member's account read, the deadline capped by the close, «În afara locurilor»; the full race — unconfirmed or wrongly named raises refused with nothing written, exactly the named places added and audited, a free place used first; the refusals by name and the Organizer; the link — the GET reads and leaves the token unspent, the secret nowhere at rest, the press seats the registration with the place moved and nobody offered, no verification email, single use, a refused form leaving the link working, an outside invitation; expiry (the job woken and the event selected, the stamp, the line offered), resend (old link «replaced», the deadline later never earlier) and withdraw (the line offered, the link «withdrawn»); the retention. `tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts`: two Administrators inviting onto the last free place on real connections — one invitation, one refusal, then exactly one place added on the confirmed press. `tests/unit/registrations/invitations.test.ts` (new) and `tests/unit/diagnostics/owner-tasks.test.ts` (the row). Updated: the sentence of §589 (`give-place*.test.ts`), the message-type tables, the static routes, the density scale, the members-only callers, the notice's length ceiling.
changelogLine: - **Invitations by email** — an Administrator invites members, partners and guests to an event from its registrations list («Invitații»): each gets one email whose link opens the registration form with their name and address filled in, and a place is kept for them until a deadline (7 days by default); on a full race the send adds one supplementary place per invitation after a confirmation that names the new capacity; «Retrimite» and «Retrage»; the privacy notice's template describes it. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: A live invitation by email that was not sent «În afara locurilor» counts as one occupied place from its send until its deadline, its acceptance or its withdrawal — compared with its deadline on every read — so the public free places and the places line drop by one per invitation, and «Cine vine» does not change (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Accepting an invitation seats the registration in the invitation's place under the event lock while the invitation still counts, then marks it accepted, so the occupied count never drops in between and nobody waiting is offered that place; on a full race a send adds one supplementary place per invitation that needs one only when the form named exactly the resulting capacity, and two Administrators inviting onto the last free place at once make one invitation and one refusal (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

An `ACCEPT_INVITATION` link is scoped to its invitation, hashed at rest and minted at the send; opening it reads in a read-only transaction and spends nothing; the form's press spends it once, a refused form takes the spend back, and a resend's newer link makes the older one read as replaced (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Only an Administrator sends, resends or withdraws invitations — asserted in the action, the admin service and the service; a send refuses, by the person's name and writing nothing, an address already registered at the event, one already invited, or a line twice; no invitation creates a registration: the invited person registers and signs themselves from the link (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

The privacy notice's template names `{{eventInvitations}}` once in each language, in the paragraph that describes the invitations by email, and `/admin/tasks` shows the row `invitationsNotice` open, never blocking, until a notice naming it is in force in every language (2026-10-02, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
